_comment: Two kinds of eval, with very different strength.
ROUTING cases score a query against every skill description by term overlap.
This is a PROXY for how the model selects a skill, not a reproduction of it:
it cannot see meaning, and it cannot see Portuguese. What it does prove is
that a description still carries its trigger vocabulary -- which is the way
descriptions actually rot. Since 2026-09-27 the six domain knowledge skills
live only in the local CoALA memory (knowledge/* records), so routing covers
the remaining task skill; domain selection is the directory -> memory key
KNOWLEDGE cases are the strong ones. Each asserts that a claim kept in the
local CoALA memory (attributed here by its memory key) still matches the
repository. When a cited symbol is renamed, the eval goes red and the record
is flagged stale instead of quietly lying.

routing.query: run the tests and check the typecheck before finishing
a test suite is flaky and fails to load a module

knowledge.claim: the route table is asserted at boot
LOG_ARGS still holds the mandatory pretty format
reads go through the silent no-optional-locks helpers
git is spawned, never shelled out
the backend test helpers still exist under server/test/helpers
index.ts is the module door and still exports GraphView
layout.ts imports no VALUE through the @/ alias -- bare Node cannot resolve it. A relative import with an explicit .ts extension is legal and is used (./paint.ts)
paint.ts stays free of value imports through the @/ alias -- the sample-svg generator loads it under bare Node
the node shapes are still described in one place, as data
CommitRow holds no radius of its own -- it reads the shapes from paint.ts
the graph runner still rewrites the tracked sample svg
the linearity assertion the perf flake comes from is still there
drag ids are scoped, not the bare type:key the architecture doc shows
intents.ts still has no runtime imports
the endpoint allowlist still exists
the app-specific surface tokens are still defined
destructive still selects hold-to-confirm
context menus are still built at click time by the shell store
pt.ts is still the untyped master that defines the key set
the other locales are still annotated, which is what makes tsc enforce both directions
the backend still translates at the edge with a passthrough fallback
all five test commands still exist
npm test still excludes the e2e suite
the e2e script is still hermetic against a temp fixture
